examples.worked_solution:
Given the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14057898/assets/35814ac6d965ac688907d162b45d9b0b194ea40375d4e474466e4fb4b1de1c1b.png) we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-8 & -5 \\ -3 & -6 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-8x-5y \\ -3x-6y \\ -4x+5y\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5y-8x \\ -3x-6y \\ 5y-4x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14057898/assets/f59824c26875665fcbd8adfc5414fa7b0c60254e01f725f9ca72cf1d370a3e8b.png)

Finally, $a-b=(-5)-(-4)=-1.$

feedback.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x-3y+8z \\ x+z+2y\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1x+(-3)y+8z \\ 1x+2y+1z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x-3y+8z \\ x+z+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
